family: nested threshold MuSig2 over replicated secret sharing
attack_title: Calving Iceberg: A Same-Message Context-Splitting Group-Key Recovery Attack
attack_result: Recovery of the Iceberg group signing key followed by an ordinary fresh-message BIP340 forgery
attack_technique: Use one corrupt member and one same-SID, same-message response from each of three honest members under distinct attacker-controlled outer MuSig2 nonce contexts; interpolate three complete group partials and solve for the two reused nonce scalars and group secret
conditions: The Figure 3 game binds one message to a SID but consumes state per honest member and does not bind the complete adversary-chosen outer context across members
affected_parameters: Iceberg t=2, n=4, mu=3, nu=2 over secp256k1 with BIP327/BIP340 and a 32-byte SID
One static corrupt member, one signing query to each of the three honest members, and three distinct outer cosigner nonce contexts
nrec_acknowledgement: The computations were performed on the Norwegian Research and Education Cloud (NREC), using resources provided by the University of Bergen and the University of Oslo.

ai_provenance.title: OpenAI Codex generated and selected the title and deliberately chose Calving Iceberg as scheme-related wordplay

scope_limitations: The executed source-backed endpoint is the paper's concrete t=2, n=4 secp256k1 profile.

The result targets the paper's formal unforgeability game and does not evaluate Lightning consensus, availability, privacy, DKG integration, or channel-state safety beyond the stated signing interface.
The attack-history statement is bounded to public material located through 18 October 2026.
